bibliography.abstract: This manuscript is an English translation and extended version of a paper originally published in Japanese (2022). Driven by remarkable advances in remote sensing and big data processing, spatial technologies are increasingly leveraged in economic research. While satellite nighttime light intensity is widely recognized for tracking macroeconomic parameters - such as regional GDP, employment, and population - less attention has been paid to fine-grained spatial processing methodologies for local tourism economies. This study first details a raster processing technique applied to nightlight imagery. It then focuses on Yuzawa Town (Uonuma District, Niigata Prefecture), analyzing the local economy and sports/tourist attractions. Specifically, I investigate the spatio-temporal relationships between tourist arrivals and various local statistical datasets. Furthermore, this paper highlights how nightlight data can capture intra-municipal economic dynamics that remain undetectable through standard macroeconomic indicators.
bibliography.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. Published in IPSJ Journal, Vol. 63, No. 3, pp. 733-741 (2022)
bibliography.title: The Potential of Nighttime Light Imagery for Detailed Local Economic Analysis

en.caveats: The empirical analysis is limited to a single small town focused on sports and tourism, which may limit the direct generalizability of the specific spatio-temporal relationships to other municipal contexts.
en.what: This study details a raster processing technique for satellite nighttime light intensity imagery and applies it to Yuzawa Town in Niigata Prefecture, Japan. It analyzes the spatio-temporal relationships between tourist arrivals, local sports and tourist attractions, and various local statistical datasets.
en.why: The method demonstrates that nighttime light data can capture fine-grained, intra-municipal economic dynamics and tourism activity that standard macroeconomic indicators fail to detect.
